title: A chat template was configured and the run recorded that it was not applied
detects: A run whose normalised record names a chat template, or asks for one, while also recording that the prompts went to the model raw. Every number from that run describes an instruction-tuned model answering prompts in a format it was never trained on, which is not the model anybody meant to measure.
incident: Ours, 2026-08-21. `--chat-template` was dead on the abliterate path: the flag parsed, the value was carried, and nothing applied it. It was found by a dead-flag audit, and the first version of that audit PASSED a tree with the bug deliberately reinstated, because it compared the flag against the tokeniser's own field of the same name rather than against what the run did.
remedy: Re-run with the template actually applied, and compare. If the figures move, the previous ones describe a different experiment. Check the field your harness writes to record the rendered prompt, not the field that records the requested setting: the defect is exactly that the two disagree.
false_positive: A base model with no chat template is supposed to take raw prompts, and a run that deliberately measures the raw format is a legitimate arm rather than a mistake. This check fires on the DISAGREEMENT between naming a template and recording that none was applied, so it stays quiet when nothing named one. It will still fire wrongly on a harness that records `chat_template_applied: false` to mean "the model supplies its own", which is a spelling no adapter here knows about. It is also silent on lm-evaluation-harness, which records the request inside `model_args` rather than as a field, so absence of a finding there means nothing.
